decision: Create a new v2 planning ledger for the Native Goal Runtime / Goal Mode feature and register it as an active, ready-for-plan-compile ledger.

Treat native Goal Mode as the replacement for the failed long prompt-packet pipeline for long/large/cross-referential work. The old prompt packets and D2 slicing are retired design constraints, not the product foundation.
Design one native Goal runtime engine with invisible internal product goals and visible assistant-chat goals as separate presentations of the same execution system.
Do not build or document a separate bootstrapped Goal Mode for the current bootstrap process because Codex app Goal Mode is available for bootstrap compile runs.
Make Goal Mode general-purpose for assistant chat, covering bugs, features, tests-until-pass, refactors, docs, repo research, migrations, audits/repairs, and planning/doc transfer.

For lower-quality models, rely on bounded worker authority, role separation, coverage/evidence, deterministic validators, stronger verification/adjudication, and runtime-owned completion rather than trusting the worker to judge global completion.
Treat document sharding as access/recovery/verification infrastructure while preserving whole-goal coherence and full source/target universe awareness.

Make assistant-chat Goal Mode visibly controllable through button/chip/icon, /goal, natural language activation, status indicator, task tracker, pause/resume/stop, edit/update, subgoal tree, and evidence/log disclosure.
Support parent goals that can spawn parallel child goals/subagents, give each child a dedicated goal/objective, and synthesize results centrally under parent merge/completion authority.

Adopt Codex v0.140-style attachment preservation as a native PM requirement: oversized objectives, large pasted blocks, and image attachments must be materialized into runtime-readable goal attachments, including remote sessions.
Defer full Chain Wizard redesign and plan graph build design until the Goal Runtime System is compiled; current Chain Wizard docs are incomplete legacy context.

Compile this ledger into a new Goal Runtime/System plan document plus necessary consumer PlanUnit updates, without creating WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, generated indexes, shards, Spec Lock, evidence bundles, or governance artifacts during this ledger phase.

Adopt risk- and phase-tiered completion certification. Every goal writes a Goal Completion Receipt; mutation-heavy, Plan-writing, ledger-transfer, test-until-pass, schema/contract, migration, destructive, and governance-sensitive goals require stronger replayable evidence and independent/deterministic verification where available.

Material mid-goal user changes create an explicit Goal Replan Event. The runtime pauses scheduling, computes impact, re-steers or cancels child goals, updates the visible task list, then resumes; trivial clarifications may apply inline, hard constraints apply immediately, and forks are reserved for alternate paths or material conflicts.

Child goals are first-class runtime objects with their own status, budgets, task lists, recovery state, and completion receipts. They are collapsible in assistant chat rather than hidden, and the parent goal owns synthesis, merge, final verification, and parent completion.

Use frozen snapshots for evidence and certification while using live state for active editing. Objective bundles and referenced attachments freeze at goal creation; read/evaluation inputs freeze at phase or certification boundaries; coding goals record start state, checkpoints, diffs, and test state identities.

Default child-goal write authority is read_only or proposal_only. Parallel direct writes require isolated worktrees or explicit non-overlapping write scopes; if two child goals need the same file, the parent serializes or isolates the work.

Goal Mode settings must expose two separate model selections: a worker model and a verifier/adjudicator model. The verifier/adjudicator model is configured separately from ordinary worker execution; provider-specific default tier mappings remain deferred.

Verifier/adjudicator may inherit the worker model only when the inherited model satisfies the required policy for the goal certification tier. Low-risk goals can inherit by default; standard and strong-certification goals use policy-derived verifier/adjudicator requirements; strong-certification goals block, not merely warn, when the requirement cannot be met.

Escalation triggers include incomplete/stale/non-replayable evidence, conflicting child outputs, repeated retries/blockers, strong-certification surfaces, destructive/governance actions, low worker confidence, out-of-scope writes, validator failures, and unsupported completion claims.

Verifier unavailable behavior is tiered: low-risk goals may finish with a degraded receipt; standard goals may degrade only when no mutation or required check is affected; strong-certification goals become blocked, not complete.

Explicit user approval is required for destructive actions, governance seal, broad writes outside declared scope, external paid/network side effects, production-affecting actions, data deletion/migration, dependency/license/security-policy changes, and credential/secrets touching. Invisible internal goals use predeclared authority and block when outside it.

Evidence retention keeps hashes, summaries, changed files, command identities, validator outputs, child receipts, verifier/adjudicator decisions, and source-to-target mappings where relevant. Raw logs are capped, redacted, separately stored, and referenced by hash/path.
Child goals default to read_only/proposal_only. Direct writes require isolated worktree, explicit non-overlapping scope, or parent-granted single-writer lease.

After the locked policy-default hardening pass, the Goal Runtime ledger has no additional product-level blockers for implementation readiness. The remaining deferred questions are implementation-owner choices or future compiler-contract work, not blockers to starting implementation planning; governance seal remains a separate explicit phase.

Goal Runtime governance seal registers Plans/Goal_Runtime_System.md as the strict canonical_plan_target, refreshes generated governance artifacts, preserves blocked_compiler_contract_incomplete node readiness, and creates no node/build/product implementation artifacts.
